headline: Diesel stays punishingly tight as Ryazan refinery fires and EPA weighs RFS exemptions
intro: Oil whipsawed this week — biggest one-day drop since April, then a 1.5-2% bounce — but the real story is diesel, which refuses to get cheaper no matter which way crude swings. Refiners keep tilting yields toward distillate and jet, Ukraine keeps hitting Russian refineries, and EPA's biofuel exemption fight is entering the homestretch.
overview: Crude and products rebounded Thursday after Wednesday's steep selloff, as fresh attacks in the Middle East and Ukraine's drone strikes on Russia's Ryazan refinery dashed hopes for near-term de-escalation. Diesel cracks remain extraordinarily wide (over $100/bbl) and US stocks are at multi-year lows for this time of year, with analysts warning meaningful relief is unlikely before second-half 2027 even as wholesale prices have eased modestly. On the refining asset and policy side, Valero agreed to acquire and restart the former LyondellBasell Houston refinery (165,000 b/d), EIA data show refiners shifting yields away from gasoline toward distillate and jet fuel, and EPA's proposal to reallocate small-refinery exemption volumes into 2026-27 is drawing broad biofuel-industry support ahead of a year-end final rule.

stories.title: Oil Rebounds, Refinery Issues Mount, Diesel Stocks Tighten
stories.summary: Oil and refined product futures rose 1.5-2% Thursday, rebounding from the biggest one-day crude selloff since April, as fresh attacks in both Middle East and Ukraine wars disrupted hopes for de-escalation while diesel stocks continue to tighten.

stories.title: How Long Until Diesel Relief? Not This Winter, and Probably Not Before the Second Half of 2027
stories.summary: Diesel is running $6.26/gal, $2.55 above a year ago, with US stocks at the lowest level for this time of year in EIA records; meaningful relief is unlikely before the second half of 2027 despite some recent easing in wholesale prices.

stories.title: Refineries have shifted production away from gasoline to middle distillates
stories.summary: EIA data through August show refinery gasoline yields have fallen significantly in 2026 as refiners shift output toward distillate fuel oil and jet fuel amid unusually high middle-distillate margins.

stories.title: NYMEX Overview: Oil Futures Rebound From Sharp Selloff as Traders Weigh Iran Diplomacy -- OPIS
stories.summary: Oil futures rebounded from a sharp selloff as traders weighed Iran diplomacy; the Brent timespread premium narrowed to under $2.50/bbl from over $5/bbl in mid-October, per MUFG.

stories.title: Does the blue wave mean lower gasoline and diesel prices soon? Don't hold your breath
stories.summary: A new Democratic Congress could pressure the administration on Iran policy, but has limited direct ability to affect gasoline and diesel prices, which remain tied to global oil market dynamics.

stories.title: Oil Up on Market Risks Despite US Congressional Shifts
stories.summary: Crude futures rebounded Thursday after their steepest one-session drop in seven months, as traders weighed continued vulnerability of oil supplies despite the US election outcome.

stories.title: Valero Energy To Acquire Former LyondellBasell Houston Refinery For $320.5 Million And Restart 165,000 Barrels Per Day Of Capacity
stories.summary: Valero agreed to acquire the former LyondellBasell Houston refinery for $320.5 million and plans to restart 165,000 b/d of capacity.

stories.title: Attack appears to hit Russia's Ryazan oil refinery, Reuters analysis finds
stories.summary: Reuters video analysis confirms Russia's Ryazan refinery, one of its largest, was hit in the latest Ukrainian drone attack.

stories.title: Renewed Refinery Attacks Deplete Russian Diesel Supply as US Deal in Focus
stories.summary: Renewed Ukrainian strikes on Russian refineries are deepening Moscow's domestic fuel shortages even as it continues diesel exports to international markets under a deal involving the US.

stories.title: EIA: US crude oil inventories down 900,000 bbl
stories.summary: EIA reported US crude oil inventories fell 900,000 bbl to 409.8 million bbl, 4% below the five-year seasonal average.

stories.title: JPMorgan sees global oil market return to surplus
stories.summary: JPMorgan says the global oil market returned to surplus in September as Middle East exports recovered and demand softened, diverging from IEA's view of a continued deficit.

stories.title: Biofuel Groups Push EPA to Protect Farm Demand as Refiners Report Strong Profits
stories.summary: Biofuel groups at an EPA hearing reiterated support for the agency's proposal to reallocate small-refinery exemption volumes, arguing farmers need relief even as refiners report strong profits.

stories.title: Clean Fuels supports US EPA’s proposal to reallocate SREs in 2026-’27
stories.summary: Clean Fuels Alliance backs EPA's proposal to reallocate small-refinery exemptions for 2026-27, saying a final rule by year-end is needed to support farmers and biofuel investment.

stories.title: Chevron produces record amount of biobased diesel in August
stories.summary: Chevron's biodiesel and renewable diesel production topped 50 million gallons in August, the first month in company history to cross that threshold.

# Chevron (CVX) 10-Q Q3 2026 — Refined Fuels Market Read

- **Refining margins surged on geopolitical supply disruption**: Total Downstream earnings jumped to $4.93B in Q3 2026 vs. $1.14B in Q3 2025 (+$3.8B), driven almost entirely by higher margins on refined product sales ($2.9B US + $1.1B international) tied to global refined-product supply disruptions from the escalating Middle East conflict. Management explicitly flags these elevated margins as potentially non-recurring ("current margin levels may not be indicative of future results").

- **US refining running near capacity, record reliability**: US refinery crude unit inputs rose to 1,093 MBD (+29 MBD, +3% YoY) in Q3, described as operating "reliably at record levels near capacity." US refined product sales were flat (1,304 vs 1,303 MBD), suggesting utilization gains are feeding exports/inventory rather than domestic demand growth.

- **International volumes contracting from conflict disruption, not demand**: International refined product sales fell sharply — down 129 MBD (-9%) in Q3 and 75 MBD (-5%) over 9M — attributed to Middle East-driven supply disruption, while international crude unit inputs were roughly flat in Q3 but down 22 MBD (-3%)

decks.analysis:
# Aemetis (AMTX) 10-Q Analysis — Q3 2026 (Period Ended Sept 30, 2026)

## Key Takeaways

- **Ethanol throughput & margins improving but credit-dependent:** Keyes Plant sold 15.6M gallons ethanol at $2.34/gal (Q3) vs. 14.7M gallons at $2.13/gal (Q3 2025); 9-month volumes rose to 44.9M gallons at $2.18/gal. California Ethanol swung to $7.4M gross profit (Q3) from a $(1.4)M loss a year ago, but $4.6M of that quarter's profit was Section 45Z PTC income — absent the credit, margins remain thin given corn costs rose to $6.29/bushel (Q3) from $5.95/bushel.

- **RNG segment driven almost entirely by tax credits, with a one-time true-up:** California Dairy RNG revenue surged to $25.9M (Q3) from $4.0M a year ago, but $20.1M was Section 45Z PTC income, including an $11.0M cumulative true-up from a September 2026 45ZCF-GREET model revision that retroactively lowered the segment's emissions rate (covering Jan–Jun 2026). Core RNG/RIN/LCFS sales (ex-PTC) were only $5.9M for the quarter — the PTC regime, not physical volumes, is the primary earnings driver, and the true-up signals volatility/non-recurring risk in future PTC recognition.

- **RIN/LCFS exposure is modest and price-sensitive:** Sold 1.4M D3 RINs at $2.45 (Q3 2026) vs. 1.0M at $2.37 (Q3 2025); LCFS credits sold at $73/credit (Q3 2026) vs. $54 (Q3 2025) — a ~35% YoY price increase, attributed partly to CARB's July 2025 LCFS amendments tightening oversupply. Company still has 5 of 12 operating digesters on lower "temporary" LCFS pathways pending CARB provisional approval, representing unrealized credit upside.

- **No active SAF/RD production — project remains in development:** The Riverbank SAF/RD plant (90M gal/yr combined SAF/RD capacity) has permits (CEQA, Use Permit, Authority to Construct) but is still in financing/engineering phase with no stated construction completion timeline or capex disclosed as committed; it sits in the non-reportable "All Other" segment with no revenue contribution.

- **Capital structure signals severe liquidity strain, limiting growth capacity:** Total debt is $435.4M (77% current/due-on-demand), short-term construction funding jumped to $35.6M from $17.4M, and the company reiterated a **going concern** doubt. Capex of $35.3M (9-month) went primarily to RNG digesters ($17.4M) and Keyes MVR energy-efficiency project ($17.1M) — not new refined-fuels capacity — reflecting a defensive capital posture focused on existing asset optimization over expansion.

- **India Biodiesel in structural decline:** Revenue fell 26% YoY (9-month) to $21.5M on lower OMC tender volumes (17.2K MT at $1,065/MT vs. 21.0K MT at $1,117/MT) and delayed contract timing — a smaller, non-U.S. credit-exposed business showing margin recovery (lower feedstock costs) but shrinking volume.

## Market Signal

Aemetis's results underscore that near-term refined-fuels/biofuels profitability is now almost entirely a function of federal Section 45Z PTC monetization and LCFS credit pricing rather than physical production economics, while heavy reliance on on-demand senior debt and a going-concern qualification signal that smaller renewable fuel producers face capital constraints that could slow RNG/SAF capacity additions even as credit values rise.

## Sunoco LP 10-Q (Q3 2026) — Refined Fuels Markets Takeaways

- **Refinery utilization strong but mixed vs. YTD**: Burnaby Refinery (55,000 bpd capacity, acquired via Parkland) ran at 99% crude utilization / 105% composite in Q3 2026, but only 78%/83% for the 9-month period, with crude throughput of 54 Mbpd (Q3) vs 43 Mbpd (9mo) — signaling a ramp-up through the year post-acquisition. Bio-feedstock throughput was modest (3 Mbpd Q3, 2 Mbpd 9mo), suggesting limited renewable co-processing rather than dedicated SAF/renewable diesel capacity; no RIN/LCFS-specific disclosures or credit monetization detail provided.

- **Fuel distribution capture rates widened materially**: Motor fuel profit margin rose to 16.8¢/gal in Q3 2026 (vs 10.7¢/gal Q3 2025) and 16.9¢/gal for 9mo (vs 10.9¢/gal), even as volumes nearly doubled (4,197M gallons Q3 vs 2,295M) — mostly Parkland-driven scale, indicating improved wholesale/retail capture rather than just volume growth.
